observations.observation: NAP operators wanted compatibility with general data portals; a substantial part of mobility data requires authentication or agreement, so metadata should describe the conditions rather than assuming open data.
SEMIC experts described collaborative governance, documented obligation levels, value vocabularies, identifiers and extension rules; existing definitions should be reused and additions reviewed.
Operators observed that some datasets, such as weather, cannot be tied to a transport mode; multiple selections and absence of a mode need consideration.
A single GTFS or NeTEx package can carry several categories, including operational and fare information; one category may be insufficient.
Operators questioned whether coverage should refer to the infrastructure or the service using it and requested clearer semantics and consistency with transport-mode choices.
Feedback distinguished the period a feed is delivered from the time interval represented by its content, such as a timetable.
Feedback distinguished update intervals at the original provider from refresh intervals exposed by the NAP.
Operators found the existing licence/contract choices insufficient to represent common licences and proposed richer access-condition distinctions.
Stakeholders sought a DCAT-AP-compatible successor to CMC, with broader engagement and sustained maintenance beyond an individual project.
SPRINT prototype experience stressed assurance, handling data/metadata versions, conditions on asset access and spatial or temporal granularity.
